title: Dynamical vertex approximation for retarded interactions: Application to the Hubbard-Holstein model
authors: Emin Moghadas, Samuele Giuli, Massimo Capone, Alessandro Toschi
abstract: We extend the dynamical vertex approximation (D$Γ$A), in its most commonly used ladder-version, to systems with retarded electronic interactions. Such an extended scheme, which we name "dynamical-$U$ D$Γ$A", allows us to study strongly interacting electrons coupled to bosons including non-local spatial correlations on all length scales on top of the purely local ones captured by dynamical mean-field theory. We demonstrate the applicability of the method in the specific case of the coupling to a single dispersionless phononic mode, by studying the Hubbard-Holstein model on the square and cubic lattices, focusing on regimes of sizable Hubbard interactions where strong electronic correlations compete with phonon-mediated interactions. As illustrative examples, we consider the antiferromagnetic phase in the three-dimensional model and the d-wave superconductor in two dimensions, analyzing the effect of the electron-phonon coupling, including its frequency dependence, on both instabilities.
summary: This work develops an advanced theoretical tool, the "dynamical-U DΓA," to handle electron-boson coupling in strongly correlated systems. By applying it to the Hubbard-Holstein model, the authors investigate how phonon-mediated interactions compete with electronic correlations to determine magnetic and superconducting ground states.
main_problem: The paper aims to extend the Dynamical Vertex Approximation (DΓA) to accurately treat strongly interacting electrons coupled to bosons, specifically addressing the frequency dependence of the interactions.
main_result: The developed "dynamical-U DΓA" scheme successfully applies to the Hubbard-Holstein model, allowing the study of how electron-phonon coupling modifies competing electronic instabilities like antiferromagnetism and d-wave superconductivity.
method: The core method is the "dynamical-U DΓA," which extends the ladder-DΓA formalism by incorporating the frequency dependence of the bare interaction into the Bethe-Salpeter equation and self-energy calculations.
model_or_system: The primary model is the Hubbard-Holstein model, which describes strongly correlated electrons (Hubbard repulsion $U$) coupled to bosonic excitations (phonons, $\Omega_\alpha$). This setup allows studying the competition between electronic correlations and electron-phonon coupling.
key_observables: Antiferromagnetic phase diagram (3D), d-wave superconducting instability (2D), magnetic fluctuations, and nonlocal electronic self-energy.
important_parameters: Hubbard interaction strength ($U$), electron-phonon coupling strength ($g$), and the characteristic phonon frequency ($\omega_0$).
main_assumptions: The method builds upon DMFT by systematically including non-local correlations via the vertex corrections, extending previous DΓA applications that assumed instantaneous interactions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the dynamical-U ladder-DΓA approach, showing the inclusion of frequency dependence in the vertex corrections.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the need to extend DΓA for retarded interactions, details the "dynamical-U DΓA" formalism by incorporating frequency dependence into the BSE and SDE, and then applies this framework to analyze the Hubbard-Holstein model's phase diagram and superconducting properties.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the treatment of retarded interactions and the systematic inclusion of bosonic coupling into a many-body self-energy framework (DΓA) shares conceptual parallels with open quantum systems where environmental coupling (bath) dynamics are crucial.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic illustration of the dynamical-U ladder- DΓA algorithm flow. The impurity vertex Γ, obtained by inverting a local BSE (upper panel), serves as the input for the lattice ladder equation (middle panel) for the full vertex Fq. This object inherits its momentum-dependence from the lattice bubble-diagrams that propagate the transfer momen- tum q. In the final step the non-local correction to the DMFT self-energy is computed via the SDE (lower panel) with the DMFT ladder vertices Fq as main building blocks.

FIG. 2. Comparison of λ-corrected (red) and uncorrected DΓA (green) self-energies on the Fermi-surface with the local DMFT self-energy (black) along with the exact self-energy 1/ν tail (gray dashed line). The data are obtained for the 3D Hubbard-Holstein model at U = 3, λ = 1, ω0 = 0.1, n = 0.9 and β = 100.

FIG. 3. DMFT and ladder-DΓA results for the N´eel temper- ature TN of the HHM on the cubic lattice as a function of λ and the three phonon frequencies ω0 = {0.1, 1, ∞}. The Hubbard interaction is fixed to U = 2.

FIG. 4. Temperature dependence of the DMFT (upper row) and ladder-DΓA (lower row) spin susceptibilities at the ordering vector Q for various fillings and the three phonon frequencies ω0 = {0.1, 1, ∞}. For all calculations considered here the Hubbard interaction is set to U = 3 with the el-ph coupling being λ = 1

FIG. 5. Doping dependence of the DMFT (red) and ladder-DΓA (green) N´eel temperature TN for ω0 = 0.1 (left panel), ω0 = 1 (middle panel) and ω0 = ∞(right panel), with U = 3 and λ = 1. Empty markers indicate incommensurate ordering vectors for the spin response, Q = (π, π, π −δ). The incommensurability δ as a function of filling n for each case is shown in the respective insets.
